questions.question: Discuss the relationship between social cooperation and successful / hunting strategies.
questions.solution_html:
• Social cooperation was essential for successful hunting strategies, as coordinated group efforts
  • allowed early humans to plan, track, and capture large or fast-moving animals more efficiently. It
  • also fostered communication, role specialization, and food sharing, strengthening social bonds and
  • ensuring group survival.

questions.question: Compare the salient features of the military systems of Sparta and / Athens Part D ESSAY QUESTION
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Examine the factors that facilitated the growth of the Roman agrarian / economy and analyze the causes underlying its eventual decline
questions.solution_html:
• The growth of the Roman agrarian economy was facilitated by fertile Mediterranean lands, advanced
  • irrigation, slave labour, and the expansion of trade networks. Over time, large estates (latifundia)
  • replaced small farms, creating economic inequality and rural depopulation. Its eventual decline
  • resulted from overreliance on slave labour, soil exhaustion, heavy taxation, and political instability
  • that disrupted agricultural productivity.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how did the reciprocity, tolerated theft and immediate return / system sustained equality in Palaeolithic groups?
questions.solution_html:
• Reciprocity in Palaeolithic groups ensured that food and resources were shared among members
  • preventing accumulation and fostering cooperation. Tolerated theft allowed individuals to take small
  • portions from others without conflict, discouraging hoarding. The immediate return system, where
  • resources were consumed soon after acquisition, prevented inequality and maintained social balance
  • within the group.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the rise and development of the Shang civilization with / reference to Erlitou, Erligang and Anyang
questions.solution_html:
• The rise of the Shang civilization can be traced to the Erlitou culture (c. 1900–1500 BCE), which
  • shows early state formation with bronze casting, palatial architecture, and social stratification. The
  • Erligang phase (c. 1500–1300 BCE) marked the expansion of urban centers like Zhengzhou
  • advancement in bronze technology, and the establishment of a centralized political system. The
  • Anyang phase (c. 1300–1046 BCE) represented the mature Shang state, with well-planned cities
  • royal tombs, oracle bone inscriptions, and a complex ritual system. Together, these phases reflect the
  • gradual evolution from a regional chiefdom to a fully developed early Chinese civilization.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critically examine the factors that contributed to the decline and / eventual failure of the Delian League
questions.solution_html:
• The Delian League, initially formed to defend Greek city-states against Persia, declined as Athens
  • transformed it into an imperial instrument serving its own interests. The misuse of league funds
  • imposition of Athenian control, and suppression of member revolts bred resentment among allies.
  • Continuous wars, especially the Peloponnesian War, exhausted resources and exposed the fragility
  • of Athenian dominance. Ultimately, the defeat of Athens by Sparta in 404 BCE marked the League’s
  • collapse, revealing that imperial overreach and loss of mutual trust undermined its original purpose.
questions.final_answer: collapse, revealing that imperial overreach and loss of mutual trust undermined its original purpose
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
